open_points.subject: clock access by run_graph
open_points.text: `clock.kernel_now` lists `module:run_graph` as a caller, while the conventions say “`run_graph` reads no clock” and `run_graph`’s module contract says “no clock — the time of a draft is the `now` `runs` passes.”
open_points.question: May `run_graph` call `clock.kernel_now`, or must every call receive its time exclusively through `plan_run.now`?
options: Remove `module:run_graph` from the clock callers and require `runs` to pass `now`
Allow `run_graph` to read the clock and remove the passed `now` rule
open_points.default_guess: Require `runs` to pass `now`; `run_graph` does not call the clock.

open_points.subject: unreadable, partial, or oversized runner report
open_points.text: `read_runner_report` says “an unreadable or partial report is not decoded into outputs” but its Outputs list has no malformed, partial, or over-bound result and its Errors section says `None`.
open_points.question: What exactly does `read_runner_report` return when framing is invalid, the report is partial, or the channel bound is exceeded, and how can `sandbox` distinguish that result from a valid report with no outputs?
options: Return a distinct invalid-report result for `sandbox` to classify as `crashed`
Return a synthetic escaped-exception report
Raise an internal error
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct invalid-report result which `sandbox` classifies as `crashed`.

open_points.subject: runner-report termination information
open_points.text: The input is “Every byte the runner wrote … until the channel closed, the environment ended, or the channel bound was passed,” with no indication of which condition stopped the read.
open_points.question: Must the caller pass the termination condition or an over-bound flag, or must report framing alone distinguish a complete report from bytes truncated because the environment ended or the bound was passed?
options: Pass the termination condition and over-bound flag
Require a self-delimiting complete frame and treat absence of its terminator as partial
Treat every collected byte sequence alike
open_points.default_guess: Pass the termination condition or over-bound flag and also validate a complete frame.

open_points.subject: re-writing an existing derived StoredValue
open_points.text: `deliver_input` says it “writes what the source still needs written” through `record_delivery_values`, but neither operation fixes what happens when the same content-derived StoredValue already exists, including after a previous delivery write survived while later run progress did not.
open_points.question: Does delivery return an existing equal StoredValue without a store change, make `record_delivery_values` an idempotent no-op for it, or treat the existing identity as an invariant failure?
options: Read and return the existing equal StoredValue without a change
Allow `record_delivery_values` to return the existing record idempotently
Return `internal_error` for an existing identity
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing equal StoredValue without writing another record.

open_points.subject: record_delivery_values duplicate semantics
open_points.text: The new `record_delivery_values` row says only that it writes derived StoredValues; the general store text says it checks “unique and existing identities” but does not say whether an already-existing equal content-derived identity is success, a no-op, or an error for this change.
open_points.question: What are the exact output and effect of `record_delivery_values` when one or all supplied StoredValues already exist with the same identity and facts?
options: Return the existing records and write nothing for them
Require every supplied record to be new
Accept an existing record only when all facts are byte-for-byte equal
open_points.default_guess: Accept and return an existing record only when all identity facts agree, writing only records that are new.

open_points.subject: empty mapped file-list reference and class
open_points.text: `empty_list_outputs` returns “a file port's empty file list — and the references the node's record names,” while an empty file list contains no SpooledFile reference on which to carry the list's disclosure class.
open_points.question: What exact reference does the NodeExecution store for an empty mapped file output, and where is that empty list's disclosure class represented?
options: Define a separate typed empty-file-list reference carrying the class
Store a value-like list record for the empty file list
Represent it as an empty SpooledFile list and add the class alongside the port entry
open_points.default_guess: Use a typed empty-file-list reference carrying its disclosure class in the NodeExecution output entry.

open_points.subject: resolved not_applied element before fresh approval is recorded
open_points.text: `operation_element_conclusion` says `not reached` applies “when the element has no NodeExecution yet” and an `owner_approval` wait includes the requested `approval_id`; recovery nevertheless requires an attempt resolved `not_applied` to be reached again when its fresh approval was never requested. Such an element already has its `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution but has no requested fresh approval.
open_points.question: What conclusion does the operation return in the crash window after `resolve_attempt(not_applied)` commits and before the fresh approval is requested, so recovery knows to reach the element without inventing an `approval_id`?
options: A distinct `needs_fresh_approval` or `not_reached_for_next_attempt` conclusion
`owner_approval` waiting with no approval id
`not reached` even though an earlier NodeExecution exists
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct conclusion meaning that the next attempt must be reached to request fresh approval.

open_points.subject: fields of derived skip and upstream-failure drafts
open_points.text: `plan_run` returns “the `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` records that became determined, as drafts” and receives `now`, but it does not fix the draft values for `started_at`, `ended_at`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `executed`, `resources_used` or `failure_detail`.
open_points.question: Which complete NodeExecution fields must each kind of draft contain, and do both `started_at` and `ended_at` equal the supplied `now`?
options: Both timestamps are `now`; executed, inputs, outputs, resources and detail are absent
Both timestamps are `now`; already available inputs are recorded
The draft omits timestamps and `runs` fills them
open_points.default_guess: Set both timestamps to `now` and leave executed, inputs, outputs, resources and failure detail absent.

open_points.subject: plan result action precedence
open_points.text: `plan_run` returns drafts, the next ready node, waiting points, outputs and status together, while the conventions require drafts to be written “in that very change”; it does not state whether a returned ready node may be executed before those drafts are persisted or whether the caller must write and re-plan first.
open_points.question: When one plan contains newly determined drafts and also identifies a ready node, what exact action must `runs` take first?
options: Write drafts and derived run state, then call `plan_run` again before executing
Write drafts, then execute the ready node from the same plan
Execute the ready node and include the drafts in the later progress change
open_points.default_guess: Write the drafts and derived run state first, then re-plan before executing another node.

open_points.subject: representation of a mapped-list ceiling failure
open_points.text: `plan_run` enforces “a mapped list over `stored_value_bytes_max` failing its node with no record,” but its Outputs do not identify a distinct node-level derived failure, the offending output port, or its failure detail.
open_points.question: How is this recordless failure represented in the plan's node conclusion and run answer, and does it carry `value_too_large` or identify an output port?
options: A derived failed-node conclusion with detail `value_too_large` and the first offending port
A derived failed-node conclusion with no detail or port
An ordinary `contract_violation` draft despite the text saying no record
open_points.default_guess: Return a recordless failed-node conclusion with `value_too_large` and the first offending output port in deterministic order.

open_points.subject: record_flow_output behavior for an already-written source
open_points.text: `record_flow_output` says “Write the value a produced flow output still needs written” and gives `record_delivery_values` as its state impact, but its source may already be a written StoredValue and the operation does not say whether it then performs a store change or simply returns that reference.
open_points.question: For each allowed source kind, when does `record_flow_output` write `record_delivery_values`, and what does it do when the source is already a written StoredValue?
options: Only persist an unwritten mapped value list; otherwise return the existing reference
Always invoke `record_delivery_values`, idempotently
Refuse any source other than an unwritten mapped value list
open_points.default_guess: Persist only an unwritten mapped value list and otherwise return the existing reference unchanged.

set_aside.subject: measurement of mapped file-output lists
set_aside.text: `assemble_mapped_lists` must “measure them against the stored value ceiling” and says “Every delivered list of the node is measured,” but a file list is only “the reference to the elements' files”; no canonical bytes whose size is measured are defined for that reference.
set_aside.question: Does `stored_value_bytes_max` apply to a mapped file-output list, and if so, what exact bytes are measured?
options: Do not apply the StoredValue ceiling to file lists; their files use spool ceilings
Measure canonical JSON of the SpooledFile references
Measure the sum of file contents
set_aside.default_guess: Do not apply `stored_value_bytes_max` to file lists; enforce only the spool ceilings on their files.

set_aside.subject: several oversized mapped value lists
set_aside.text: The output is “Every list built …; or that one list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`,” although a mapped node may have several delivered output lists and more than one may exceed the ceiling.
set_aside.question: When several delivered lists exceed the ceiling, what result identifies the failure, and in what deterministic output-port order is the first oversized list selected?
options: Return all oversized output ports
Return the first output port in code-point name order
Return an unqualified node-level over-ceiling result
set_aside.default_guess: Return the first oversized output port in code-point name order after measuring every delivered list.
